content.user_title: Embed Web Content in WinUI 3 with WebView2
content.value_statement: Embedding web interfaces in Windows desktop apps requires careful initialization, messaging, and asset packaging. This skill guides WebView2 integration with local content mapping and explicit security boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Explains virtual host mapping for local web assets with minimal cross-origin access.
Provides C# initialization and XAML loading-state examples with error-handling guidance.
Shows native-to-web and web-to-native messaging with origin checks and command authorization guidance.
Describes startup, memory, rendering, and embedded web performance practices.
Provides MSBuild and manual-copy examples for packaging built web assets.
Explains theme synchronization between XAML resources and CSS variables.
limitations: Targets WinUI 3 desktop applications, not generic browser-only React development.
Provides guidance and examples, not a complete application or automated test suite.
Requires app-defined message types, authorization handlers, asset resolution, and error interfaces.
Media loading performance and runtime-dependent behavior require testing on deployed Windows environments.

use_cases.title: Add a web dashboard to a desktop app
use_cases.description: Host a React or Vite dashboard in WinUI 3 using local asset mapping and controlled initialization.

use_cases.title: Design a restricted native message bridge
use_cases.description: Plan message types, source validation, payload limits, and authorized native commands for an embedded web interface.

use_cases.title: Package web assets for desktop releases
use_cases.description: Review build ordering, MSBuild content items, release staging, and packaged asset verification.

prompt_templates.title: Understand local content hosting
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how WebView2 hosts local web assets in WinUI 3 using virtual host mapping. Include initialization order and cross-origin access settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn the integration model before changing an application.

prompt_templates.title: Add loading and error states
prompt_templates.prompt: Help integrate WebView2 into my WinUI 3 page. Use my supplied XAML and C# to plan initialization, loading feedback, and navigation failure handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: adapt an existing page to host web content.

prompt_templates.title: Review production asset packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my supplied WinUI project and web build configuration. Check asset build ordering, output paths, publish copying, and stale asset handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: prepare embedded web assets for a desktop release.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the native message boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my supplied WebView2 message handlers and navigation rules. Check source origins, ports, payload bounds, command authorization, and sensitive outbound data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess the security boundary between web content and native capabilities.

output_examples.input: My local dashboard fails when Source is configured in XAML. What should change?
output: Initialize CoreWebView2 before configuring the virtual host mapping.
Map the built asset folder with cross-origin access denied, then navigate to the mapped index page.
Handle initialization exceptions and navigation failures with an application-owned retry state.

output_examples.input: Review the security requirements for my embedded web command bridge.
output: Accept messages only from the intended HTTPS origin and default port.
Reject malformed payloads and enforce size, shape, and command permission checks before native work.
Check the current document origin before sending sensitive data, and restrict navigation and new windows.

output_examples.input: How should I prepare web assets for a WinUI desktop release?
output: Build the web project before MSBuild evaluates asset content items.
Include built assets in build and publish output, then verify the packaged index page exists.
Use clean release staging to prevent removed assets from remaining in the package.

best_practices: Initialize CoreWebView2, configure local host mapping, and navigate only after setup succeeds.
Enforce origin checks, payload validation, and per-command authorization at the native message boundary.
Verify packaged assets and benchmark startup, memory, and media behavior against the deployed runtime.
anti_patterns: Setting Source in XAML before virtual host mapping is configured.
Exposing broad native object graphs without origin checks and command authorization.
Publishing without verifying built assets or removing stale release files.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers WebView2 integration in WinUI 3, including local content, initialization, messaging, performance, packaging, and theme synchronization.

faq.question: Does it build a complete application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that require adaptation to your application and Windows environment.

faq.question: Can I use it for a browser-only React application?
faq.answer: Its focus is embedded web content in WinUI 3. It is not intended for generic browser-only React development.

faq.question: How are local web assets loaded?
faq.answer: The examples map a local asset folder to a virtual HTTPS host after CoreWebView2 initialization.

faq.question: Does web messaging require security checks?
faq.answer: Yes. Validate message origins, payloads, and command permissions, and restrict navigation before exposing native capabilities.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production without changes?
faq.answer: No. Implement app-defined helpers and validation, verify packaged output, and test behavior against the deployed WebView2 Runtime.
